question: A coin is tossed until it lands heads; the pot starts at £2 and doubles with each tails. What should you pay to play?
answer: Its average payout is infinite: half the time £2, a quarter £4, an eighth £8, each adding £1 to the average. Yet few would pay even £20. Daniel Bernoulli answered in 1738 that each extra pound matters less the richer you are, so the pot's worth to you sets the price.
move: An average can mislead when rare, huge outcomes drive it.
ask: Which bet have I judged by its average when the rare outcomes did all the work?
source: Bernoulli, Exposition of a new theory on the measurement of risk, 1738, translated 1954
reference: Daniel Bernoulli, Exposition of a New Theory on the Measurement of Risk, translated by Louise Sommer, Econometrica 22(1):23–36, 1954
